output.title: Weekly rhythm is a scope constraint, not a calendar note
output.body:
If you run a 1-10 person business, weekly rhythm is not just a scheduling issue. It is a design constraint. A workflow only makes sense for automation or AI if it fits into a repeatable slot in your week, without forcing a new meeting, a new approval chain, or a hiring decision just to keep it alive.

The practical next step is to map one recurring task against your actual week. Note when it happens, who has to touch it, and which step still needs human judgment. If the task only appears once in a while, or if it depends on you reacting in the moment, that is a useful answer too. Not every problem deserves automation. Some deserve a better checklist, and that is fine.

If the task is regular enough, ask a narrower question: can one bounded step run inside the time you already have, while human approval stays in place for anything sensitive? That is the level where a pilot starts to look sensible.

The useful test is simple: what repeating task keeps landing in the same part of your week, and is it actually ready for a process change?
